source: RedAmon Bug Bounty Coverage taxonomy (full 22-family import, 2026-11-11), adapted as the CyberBox methodology spine

payout_scale.note: payout_rank 1..5 maps $..$$$$$ — what the class actually pays once dupe saturation and triage drift are priced in. Runs OPPOSITE to priority: a P5 primitive can be $$$$$ inside a chain.

families.name: Information Disclosure and Secrets
families.note: The finding is the credential, not the disclosure.

families.name: HTTP Desync, Caching and Proxy
families.note: Front-end/back-end parsing disagreement; cache keyed wrong.

families.name: API and GraphQL Specific
families.note: Object- and function-level authz on machine surface.

families.name: Infrastructure, DNS and Cloud
families.note: Dangling records, metadata, misconfigured buckets.

families.name: OAuth, SSO and Federation
families.note: redirect_uri, state, token confusion — account takeover surface.

families.name: AI and LLM Attack Surface
families.note: Indirect prompt injection into tool-calling agents (CWE-1427) fastest-growing scoped surface.

families.name: Supply Chain and CI/CD
families.note: Dependency confusion, runner poisoning, build-system compromise.

families.name: Cryptography and Token Handling
families.note: JWT confusion, weak secrets, predictable tokens.

families.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
families.note: Value is reaching cloud metadata / internal services, not the DNS ping.

families.name: Server-Side Injection
families.note: SQLi / RCE / SSTI at the top.

families.name: XML, Deserialization and Parser Attacks
families.note: XXE, insecure deserialization, parser differentials.

families.name: Business Logic, Race Conditions and Workflow
families.note: State machines, TOCTOU, idempotency, value extraction.

families.name: Authentication and Session Management
families.note: Password reset, session fixation, 2FA bypass.

families.name: Broken Access Control and Authorization
families.note: IDOR / BOLA / BFLA — highest paid family by concentration.

families.name: File Upload and Path Handling
families.note: Unrestricted upload, path traversal, LFI.

families.name: Cross-Site Scripting and Client-Side Injection
families.note: Highest report VOLUME, not highest payout; dupe-heavy standalone.

families.name: Cross-Origin and Browser Trust
families.note: CORS, postMessage, cookie scope, CSP bypass.

families.name: Client-Side Request and Path Manipulation
families.note: CSPT, client-side path traversal into trusted fetches.

families.name: Content Spoofing, Redirects and Impersonation
families.note: Open redirect, dangling markup — chain fuel, weak alone.

families.name: Denial of Service and Resource Abuse
families.note: Mostly out of scope; narrow exceptions, isolated instances only.

families.name: Adjacent scope worth knowing
families.note: Mobile, thick-client, binary surface bordering web scope.

families.name: Frontier classes, 2025 to 2026
families.note: Newest techniques: agentic AI, HTTP/1.1 desync endgame, CSPT2CSRF.

families.name: Chains that turn a medium into a critical
families.note: The escalation catalog. Most large payouts are 2-3 ordinary findings stacked.

families.name: Commonly closed as informational
families.note: Never report standalone — only inside a chain or when the program explicitly asks.

families.name: Reporting checklist
families.note: What moves a finding to the top of the triage queue.

classes.name: Disclosure of secrets for a publicly accessible asset
classes.signal: Live provider key/token reachable without auth.

classes.name: Disclosure of secrets for an internal asset
classes.signal: Credential for an internal-only system.

classes.name: Disclosure of known public information / intentionally public samples
classes.signal: Sample/demo data.

classes.name: Secrets in JavaScript bundles
classes.signal: Keys inlined at build; grep secret/token/key/password/apiKey.

classes.name: Exposed source maps
classes.signal: Append .map or read sourceMappingURL to recover full source.

classes.name: Exposed version control and environment files
classes.signal: /.git/config, /.env, /.svn, /.DS_Store, config.php.bak.

classes.name: Backup and temporary files
classes.signal: index.php~, .swp, .old, webroot zip, DB dump in /uploads.

classes.name: Directory listing
classes.signal: Higher when it lists something sensitive.

classes.name: Visible detailed error / debug page
classes.signal: Force a type error; unexpected content type, malformed JSON body.

classes.name: Exposed debug and management endpoints
classes.signal: Spring actuator env/heapdump, Django debug, phpinfo, Rails console, /metrics.

classes.name: Exposed portal
classes.signal: Admin portal reachable; P5 when protected.

classes.name: Exposed API schemas and introspection
classes.signal: swagger/openapi/WSDL/GraphQL introspection; hands over the surface.

classes.name: Excessive data exposure in API responses
classes.signal: Full object returned, UI hides fields; read raw JSON on profile/listing.

classes.name: Improper inventory management
classes.signal: Forgotten hosts, old versions, staging copies of prod data.

classes.name: Secrets in public repositories, CI logs, container images, mobile apps
classes.signal: Org repos, forks, gists, history, build logs, Docker layers, APK/IPA.

classes.name: Sensitive token in URL
classes.signal: Token in the address, logs, referer.

classes.name: Non-sensitive token in URL
classes.signal: Low value in URL.

classes.name: Token leakage via Referer
classes.signal: Token leaves via Referer to a third party or over HTTP.

classes.name: Sensitive token in localStorage / sessionStorage
classes.signal: Auth token in web storage reachable by XSS.

classes.name: PII leakage or exposure
classes.signal: Personal data by volume and sensitivity.

classes.name: Pay-per-use abuse from a leaked key
classes.signal: Leaked third-party key that costs the target money.

classes.name: Internal IP disclosure
classes.signal: Internal addressing leaked.

classes.name: Fingerprinting / banner disclosure, software versions in headers
classes.signal: Version/banner in responses.

classes.name: GraphQL introspection enabled
classes.signal: Schema exposed.

classes.name: Publicly accessible robots.txt with sensitive paths
classes.signal: Sensitive paths disclosed.

classes.name: Mixed content (HTTPS sourcing HTTP)
classes.signal: Insecure subresource.

classes.name: Missing Cache-Control on a sensitive page
classes.signal: Shared-browser and proxy retention of authenticated paths.

classes.name: JSON hijacking / XSSI
classes.signal: Per-user JSON loadable cross-origin.

classes.name: EXIF geolocation not stripped
classes.signal: Location/author metadata survives upload.

classes.name: Security logging and alerting failures
classes.signal: Report when you can show an attack leaves no trace.

classes.name: HTTP request smuggling, classic
classes.signal: CL.TE, TE.CL, TE.TE with obfuscated Transfer-Encoding; confirm by timing first.

classes.name: 0.CL and CL.0 desync
classes.signal: Back end treats a request as having no body while the front end does (or reverse). CVE-2025-32094.

classes.name: HTTP/2 downgrade smuggling
classes.signal: H2.CL, H2.TE, CRLF in an H2 header/pseudo-header when the edge rewrites to HTTP/1.1.

classes.name: Client-side desync
classes.signal: Victim's own browser poisons its connection; POST whose body the server ignores.

classes.name: Expect-based and obfuscation-based desync
classes.signal: Expect: 100-continue handling differences, header-name obfuscation one hop accepts.

classes.name: Web cache poisoning
classes.signal: Unkeyed input changes the cached response; X-Forwarded-Host/Scheme/Port, X-Original-URL, X-Host.

classes.name: Internal / framework cache poisoning
classes.signal: Poison a framework's own internal cache, not a CDN. Next.js stale-data/route-cache chains.

classes.name: Fat GET and parameter cloaking
classes.signal: GET with a body, semicolon separator, duplicated/unkeyed param that still reaches the app.

classes.name: Cache key normalization abuse
classes.signal: Key built from a normalized path while the origin sees the raw one, or vice versa.

classes.name: Web cache deception
classes.signal: Authenticated page under a static-looking suffix; /account/settings/x.css.

classes.name: Cache poisoning denial of service (CPDoS)
classes.signal: Oversized/malformed header the origin rejects and the cache stores, served to everyone.

classes.name: Virtual host confusion and origin exposure
classes.signal: Origin answers for internal hostnames directly, bypassing edge/WAF/auth. Find IP via CT/DNS history.

classes.name: WAF bypass via direct server access
classes.signal: Protection enforced only at the edge; origin publicly reachable.

classes.name: CDN misconfiguration
classes.signal: Auth/rate-limit only at the edge; cache serving another tenant's content; unauth purge.

classes.name: Unauthenticated internal API endpoints
classes.signal: Service-to-service routes at the public edge; /internal, /v1/admin, /api/system.

classes.name: Old API versions left unpatched
classes.signal: v1 still runs, never got v2's authz fix. Decrement the version in path/Accept/subdomain.

classes.name: Shadow endpoints from other clients
classes.signal: Mobile/desktop routes the web app does not call, with weaker checks; decompile and replay.

classes.name: Unsafe consumption of APIs
classes.signal: Target trusts a third-party API response and forwards it into a sink.

classes.name: Unrestricted resource consumption
classes.signal: No pagination ceiling/cost control; limit=1000000, negative/zero drops the clause.

classes.name: GraphQL introspection in production
classes.signal: Schema exposed; if disabled try field suggestions.

classes.name: GraphQL alias and batching abuse
classes.signal: Hundreds of aliased ops in one request defeat per-request rate limits on OTP/coupon/invite.

classes.name: GraphQL depth and complexity exhaustion
classes.signal: A relation pointing back to its parent nested deep.

classes.name: GraphQL field-level authorization gaps
classes.signal: Query authorized, individual fields are not.

classes.name: GraphQL mutations exposing admin operations
classes.signal: Admin mutation reachable by a low role.

classes.name: GraphQL injection into a downstream filter or ORM
classes.signal: Filter/arg passed verbatim into the ORM.

classes.name: Webhook signature not verified or replayable
classes.signal: Forge payment.succeeded; no timestamp means it replays forever.

classes.name: Long-lived unscoped API keys
classes.signal: Never expire, cannot rotate, full account scope accepted in a query param.

classes.name: gRPC-web / JSON transcoding gaps
classes.signal: Transcoding layer exposes methods/fields the intended surface does not.

classes.name: Subdomain takeover
classes.signal: Dangling CNAME to a deprovisioned service; look for the provider 404, then register.

classes.name: NS delegation takeover
classes.signal: Delegated zone pointing at claimable nameservers gives the whole subtree.

classes.name: Dangling A record to a reclaimable cloud IP
classes.signal: Record points at an IP you can re-provision.

classes.name: DNS zone transfer allowed (AXFR)
classes.signal: Full zone dumpable.

classes.name: Missing CAA record / missing DNSSEC
classes.signal: Weak DNS hardening.

classes.name: Bitsquatting
classes.signal: Adjacent domain registration.

classes.name: Broken link hijacking
classes.signal: Page links to an expired domain/dead handle/unclaimed package you register.

classes.name: Publicly accessible cloud storage
classes.signal: Test list/get/put and ACL; write = site takeover. Check company-named and -dev/-backup buckets.

classes.name: Unencrypted sensitive data at rest
classes.signal: Data stored without encryption.

classes.name: Publicly accessible IAM credentials
classes.signal: Live cloud credentials reachable.

classes.name: Overly permissive IAM roles
classes.signal: Enumerate the identity's permissions read-only, then stop.

classes.name: Insecure Firebase / BaaS rules
classes.signal: Default rules leave the DB readable/writable to the public project id; append /.json.

classes.name: Exposed datastores and search clusters
classes.signal: Elasticsearch, Redis, MongoDB, Kibana, Memcached, broker, metrics store without auth.

classes.name: Exposed container and orchestration APIs
classes.signal: Docker socket 2375/2376, kubelet 10250, k8s API 6443, etcd 2379, Consul 8500.

classes.name: Open management ports to the internet
classes.signal: Admin ports reachable.

classes.name: Lack of network segmentation
classes.signal: Flat network reach.

classes.name: Using default credentials
classes.signal: Shipped default login still works.

classes.name: Exposed admin panels
classes.signal: Jenkins console, Grafana, phpMyAdmin, Adminer, Airflow, RabbitMQ, vendor appliances.

classes.name: Known vulnerabilities in edge software
classes.signal: Confluence, Jira, GitLab, Citrix, Ivanti, Fortinet, Exchange, MOVEit; fingerprint the exact build.

classes.name: Outdated software version / unpatched JS libraries
classes.signal: Version number with no proof of reachability is a scanner result.

classes.name: Misconfigured file share
classes.signal: Anonymous FTP/SMB and what it exposes.

classes.name: DBMS misconfiguration, excessively privileged user
classes.signal: Over-privileged DB account.

classes.name: Mail server misconfiguration
classes.signal: Missing/misconfigured DMARC reaching the inbox; verify delivery, do not report the record alone.

classes.name: Insecure SSL/TLS
classes.signal: Cert errors, weak ciphers, no forward secrecy where actually exploitable.

classes.name: Lack of security headers
classes.signal: CSP/HSTS/X-Frame-Options/X-Content-Type-Options reported alone.

classes.name: Insecure Content-Security-Policy
classes.signal: Weak CSP alone.

classes.name: Missing Subresource Integrity
classes.signal: SRI absent; escalates when the host is abandoned.

classes.name: Potentially unsafe HTTP method enabled (OPTIONS, TRACE)
classes.signal: Methods enabled.

classes.name: Telnet enabled
classes.signal: Cleartext admin.

classes.name: Active Directory adjacent
classes.signal: Kerberoasting, ASREPRoasting, unconstrained delegation, SCCM/NTLM relay, LDAP anon bind, DACL abuse.

classes.name: Weak redirect_uri validation
classes.signal: Prefix/suffix/wildcard match; added path segment, different port/scheme, # or ? truncation.

classes.name: Missing or broken state parameter
classes.signal: No CSRF binding on the callback; drop state and see if it still completes.

classes.name: OAuth account takeover
classes.signal: Chained redirect/state/token confusion lands another user's account.

classes.name: OAuth account squatting
classes.signal: Claim an account tied to an identity the victim will later use.

classes.name: Authorization code leaked via Referer or a chained open redirect
classes.signal: Code escapes to attacker origin.

classes.name: Code replay, missing PKCE, PKCE downgrade
classes.signal: Exchange a code twice, or strip code_challenge/code_verifier from both legs.

classes.name: Implicit flow token in the URL fragment
classes.signal: Token lands in history/extensions and any script on the landing page.

classes.name: Scope escalation / consent bypass
classes.signal: Scope consented is not the scope issued; add scopes to the token request only.

classes.name: OAuth client secret hardcoded in the client
classes.signal: Rises sharply if the secret enables confidential-client flows.

classes.name: SAML signature not verified
classes.signal: Edit NameID and resubmit, or re-sign with your own certificate.

classes.name: XML signature wrapping (XSW)
classes.signal: Keep the signed assertion, nest it, add a forged assertion as a sibling the parser reads.

classes.name: SAML comment truncation
classes.signal: admin<!---->@target.com resolves to admin@target.com for one component.

classes.name: id_token audience or issuer not validated
classes.signal: A token minted by the same provider for a different app is accepted.

classes.name: Third-party access token substitution
classes.signal: App trusts a social access token without checking which client it was issued to.

classes.name: IdP-initiated flow abuse / unsolicited response accepted
classes.signal: Unsolicited SSO response accepted.

classes.name: Prompt injection, direct
classes.signal: User instruction overrides the system prompt; impact is acting as another user, not just swearing.

classes.name: Prompt injection, indirect
classes.signal: Instructions hidden in content the model reads on someone else's behalf (page, PDF, ticket, invite).

classes.name: System prompt leakage
classes.signal: Recovers instructions, tool list, internal identifiers; recon for tool abuse.

classes.name: Improper output handling
classes.signal: Model output rendered as HTML/Markdown, executed as SQL or shell; markdown image exfil is standard.

classes.name: Improper input handling
classes.signal: ANSI escapes, RTL overrides, unicode confusables reaching a terminal/reviewer UI.

classes.name: Tool and function-call abuse
classes.signal: Model can fetch URLs, read files, query DBs, run code; authz sits on the user, not the request.

classes.name: Remote code execution via an agent
classes.signal: A code-interpreter/shell tool escaping its sandbox, or reachable without confirmation.

classes.name: Excessive agency
classes.signal: Agent can send/delete/purchase/deploy without a human step; any injection becomes real-world action.

classes.name: Cross-tenant PII leakage
classes.signal: Shared cache keys, mixed session state, an over-broad memory feature, cached responses.

classes.name: Key leak
classes.signal: App calls the provider from the browser with a real key, visible in the network tab.

classes.name: Vector and embedding weaknesses
classes.signal: RAG index poisoning, cross-tenant retrieval, embedding inversion; check citations.

classes.name: Data and model poisoning
classes.signal: Backdoor/bias through a training, fine-tuning or feedback channel you can reach.

classes.name: Model extraction
classes.signal: API query-based reconstruction.

classes.name: Adversarial example injection / misclassification
classes.signal: Relevant where the model gates a security/moderation decision.

classes.name: Unbounded consumption
classes.signal: No token/request budget on an expensive model: denial of wallet.

classes.name: Insufficient rate limiting, query flooding / API token abuse
classes.signal: No throttle on model calls.

classes.name: Misinformation / wrong factual data
classes.signal: Payable only where a wrong answer carries real consequence.

classes.name: AI supply chain
classes.signal: Poisoned model artifact, malicious pickle in a checkpoint, untrusted plugin/MCP server, typosquatted model.

classes.name: Bias findings
classes.signal: Only in scope on programs that explicitly ask.

classes.name: Dependency confusion
classes.signal: Internal package name unclaimed on the public registry; find names in a lockfile/Dockerfile/error.

classes.name: Unclaimed or expired package, scope, or maintainer domain
classes.signal: Removed packages, renamed orgs, maintainer email domains available to buy.

classes.name: Typosquatting and malicious packages
classes.signal: Near-name packages with install-time scripts or a postinstall exfil hook.

classes.name: Software package takeover
classes.signal: Any path to publishing a version consumers trust.

classes.name: Missing SRI on third-party scripts
classes.signal: Escalates when the host is abandoned or the domain expires.

classes.name: Compromised or unpinned CDN script
classes.signal: Script pulled unpinned from a host you can influence.

classes.name: CI workflow injection
classes.signal: A PR title, branch name or issue body interpolated into a run: block that holds secrets.

classes.name: Untrusted pull request with secret access (pwn_request)
classes.signal: Workflow checks out fork code and runs it with repo secrets before maintainer approval.

classes.name: Self-hosted runner takeover
classes.signal: A public repo whose runner any contributor can reach, often inside a corporate network.

classes.name: Artifact and release pipeline write access
classes.signal: Write access to published artifacts; report immediately and publish nothing.

classes.name: Vulnerable dependency with a proven reachable path
classes.signal: The reachability proof is the report; a version number alone is closed.

classes.name: Software or data integrity failures
classes.signal: Unsigned updates, an auto-update channel without verification, a plugin installer trusting an unauth source.

classes.name: Predictable identifiers and tokens
classes.signal: Session/reset/invite/API/object tokens from a timestamp, counter, weak PRNG; collect a few hundred.

classes.name: Predictable or reused PRNG seed, small seed space
classes.signal: Seed guessable or reused.

classes.name: Limited RNG entropy source
classes.signal: Low-entropy generator.

classes.name: Insufficient key space
classes.signal: Brute-forceable key.

classes.name: Weak hash: lack of salt, predictable salt, insufficient key stretching
classes.signal: Unsalted/fast password hashing shown by a leak/export/API.

classes.name: Padding oracle attack
classes.signal: Distinguishable valid/invalid padding responses let you decrypt and often forge.

classes.name: Timing attack
classes.signal: Non-constant-time comparison of a token, MAC or password.

classes.name: IV reuse / predictable IV
classes.signal: Reused/guessable IV.

classes.name: ECB mode pattern leakage and CBC bit flipping
classes.signal: Identical 16-byte blocks in a base64 token; flip a block with guessable plaintext structure.

classes.name: Length extension
classes.signal: Any MAC of the form hash(secret + message) on an SHA-1/SHA-2 digest.

classes.name: Key reuse across environments
classes.signal: A staging key that verifies production tokens.

classes.name: Lack of perfect forward secrecy
classes.signal: No PFS.

classes.name: Insufficient verification of data authenticity
classes.signal: Signature verified and the result ignored, or exception caught and execution continued; tamper and see.

classes.name: Use of a broken cryptographic primitive or a vulnerable crypto library
classes.signal: Deprecated primitive or vulnerable lib in use.

classes.name: Missing cryptographic step / improper spec implementation
classes.signal: A required step skipped.

classes.name: Hardcoded password or key
classes.signal: Secret baked into shipped code.

classes.name: Use of an expired key or certificate
classes.signal: Expired material still trusted.

classes.name: Incomplete cleanup of keying material
classes.signal: Key residue left behind.

classes.name: SSRF, internal secrets exposure
classes.signal: Request reaches an internal secret.

classes.name: SSRF, internal data exposure
classes.signal: Reaches internal data.

classes.name: SSRF, internal port / service scan
classes.signal: Differential timing against open/closed internal ports.

classes.name: SSRF, external DNS query only or low impact
classes.signal: DNS callback only.

classes.name: Full-read SSRF
classes.signal: Internal response body comes back; the app is now a proxy. Point at 127.0.0.1 on internal ports.

classes.name: Blind SSRF
classes.signal: No body, but the request measurably happens; differential timing against open/closed ports.

classes.name: Blind SSRF made visible via HTTP redirect loops
classes.signal: Force the fetcher into a redirect loop whose depth/error encodes the internal response.

classes.name: Cloud metadata access
classes.signal: 169.254.169.254 (IMDSv1) returns role credentials; Azure/Alibaba/Oracle equivalents, 169.254.170.2 ECS.

classes.name: SSRF filter bypass
classes.signal: 302 to internal, DNS rebinding, decimal/octal/hex, IPv6-mapped, 0.0.0.0, user@internal, #/? truncation.

classes.name: Protocol smuggling from SSRF
classes.signal: gopher:// to write a Redis key or speak SMTP; dict://, file://, ftp://, ldap://.

classes.name: SSRF in headless renderers
classes.signal: HTML-to-PDF/screenshot/preview services fetch iframe/img/link/object; file:// local reads.

classes.name: SSRF in image and media processing
classes.signal: SVG external href, XMP references, M3U8 playlists naming an internal host.

classes.name: SSRF via webhooks and integrations
classes.signal: Designed to call a URL you supply; webhook/callback/import-by-URL/RSS/SAML ACS URL.

classes.name: SSRF via link preview / oEmbed / unfurl
classes.signal: Any feature that renders a card for a pasted URL, often with weaker network controls.

classes.name: Request splitting from SSRF
classes.signal: CRLF in a URL path the client does not encode gives a fully controlled internal request.

classes.name: HTTP/2 CONNECT port scanning
classes.signal: CONNECT over HTTP/2 against a proxy reveals internal reachable ports without a classic SSRF sink.

classes.name: SQL injection
classes.signal: Error/union-based: a quote changes the response, then ORDER BY and UNION with a matching column count.

classes.name: Blind SQL injection
classes.signal: Boolean (AND 1=1 vs AND 1=2) and time-based (SLEEP, pg_sleep, WAITFOR DELAY).

classes.name: Out-of-band SQL injection
classes.signal: DB makes a DNS/HTTP request; xp_dirtree, LOAD_FILE on UNC, UTL_HTTP.

classes.name: Second-order SQL injection
classes.signal: Stored safely, injected later when another feature reads it into a query.

classes.name: NoSQL injection
classes.signal: password[$ne]=1, {$gt:''}, $regex oracle, $where for JS execution, $lookup.

classes.name: ORM leaking / ORM injection
classes.signal: A JSON filter (select/include/orderBy) passed to the ORM verbatim; a search filter becomes a DB dump.

classes.name: OS command injection
classes.signal: Shell metacharacters reach a command in file conversion, PDF gen, network tooling; confirm blind via DNS.

classes.name: Argument injection
classes.signal: No metacharacters but you control an argument; a leading dash becomes a flag (--output=, -o, -Fconfig).

classes.name: Server-Side Template Injection
classes.signal: {{7*7}} -> 49 identifies the engine across Jinja2/Twig/FreeMarker/Velocity/ERB; error-based/blind SSTI too.

classes.name: Expression language injection (SpEL, OGNL, MVEL)
classes.signal: Reachable through a validation message or error-message interpolation path.

classes.name: Remote code execution
classes.signal: Terminal state of many of the above; verify non-destructively and stop.

classes.name: LDAP injection
classes.signal: *)(uid=*))(|(uid=* on directory-backed login and user search.

classes.name: XPath / XQuery injection
classes.signal: ' or '1'='1 then substring() extraction.

classes.name: CRLF injection / HTTP response splitting
classes.signal: %0d%0a reaching a Location, Set-Cookie, or any header echoed from a parameter.

classes.name: Host header injection
classes.signal: Absolute URLs, reset links, cache keys, and routing-based SSRF where the header picks the backend.

classes.name: HTTP parameter pollution (HPP)
classes.signal: Duplicate params parsed differently; escalates when it bypasses a filter/signature/cache key.

classes.name: Email header injection
classes.signal: Newlines in name/subject/address add Bcc/Cc or rewrite the mail body.

classes.name: Log injection and log lookup evaluation
classes.signal: Forged log entries, and on a vulnerable stack the log line is evaluated (the Log4j JNDI pattern).

classes.name: Server-side prototype pollution
classes.signal: __proto__ or constructor.prototype in a JSON body reaching a merge/clone, then a gadget.

classes.name: Server-side JavaScript injection
classes.signal: eval/Function/vm or a sandboxed runner fed request data; escape via constructor chains and process.

classes.name: File inclusion, local
classes.signal: A path parameter selecting a file to include/render; php://filter to base64 the source, /proc/self/environ.

classes.name: File inclusion, remote
classes.signal: The include target can be a URL; legacy PHP and some template loaders.

classes.name: Path traversal, server-side
classes.signal: ../, encoded and double-encoded, ....//, UTF-8 overlong, unicode normalization variants.

classes.name: CSV / formula injection
classes.signal: =cmd|' /C calc'!A0, plus +, -, @ and tab/CR prefixes in an export staff will open.

classes.name: SOAP / WSDL injection and HTTP client proxy abuse
classes.signal: An HttpWebClientProtocol chain via attacker-controlled WSDL reaches RCE.

classes.name: XXE file disclosure
classes.signal: A DOCTYPE with a SYSTEM entity reading /etc/passwd or a Windows path, echoed back.

classes.name: Blind and error-based XXE
classes.signal: External DTD you host wrapping the file into a hostname/URL path, or leaking it in a parser error.

classes.name: XInclude injection
classes.signal: You control only a fragment and cannot add a DOCTYPE, but xi:include still pulls a file.

classes.name: XXE via document formats
classes.signal: Office/design formats are zipped XML: docx, xlsx, pptx, odt, svg, plus XMP metadata in images.

classes.name: XXE via SOAP and legacy API endpoints
classes.signal: Legacy XML endpoints parsing external entities.

classes.name: Entity expansion DoS (billion laughs)
classes.signal: Nested entity expansion exhausts memory.

classes.name: Java deserialization
classes.signal: A serialized stream from a cookie/param/queue; r00AB base64 prefix, ac ed 00 05 magic. Gadget chains.

classes.name: PHP object injection
classes.signal: unserialize on request data (O:/a: prefixed), or phar:// in any path parameter reaching a filesystem op.

classes.name: Python pickle and unsafe YAML
classes.signal: pickle.loads on a session cookie/cached object, yaml.load without SafeLoader.

classes.name: .NET unsafe type handling
classes.signal: BinaryFormatter, LosFormatter, JSON.NET TypeNameHandling ($type field), a tampered ViewState without a MAC.

classes.name: Node / JavaScript deserialization
classes.signal: node-serialize style libraries evaluating an IIFE in the serialized form.

classes.name: Vulnerable media and document libraries
classes.signal: ImageMagick delegates, Ghostscript, ffmpeg playlist reads, ExifTool, LibreOffice headless conversion.

classes.name: Parser differentials
classes.signal: Two components parse the same bytes differently; JSON duplicate keys, YAML, XML, multipart, URLs, JWT segments.

classes.name: Unicode normalization bypass
classes.signal: Input validated pre-normalization and used post-normalization; fi folding, Turkish dotless i, case-folding collisions.

classes.name: Price / amount / discount tampering

informational_standalone: Missing security headers alone (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options)
Self-XSS with no delivery mechanism
Clickjacking on a page with no state-changing action
CSRF on logout, language switch, or a trivial preference
CSRF token not unique per request
Missing SPF or DMARC on a non-sending domain; spoofing that only reaches spam
Absence of rate limiting with no cost, lockout or data reached
Version and banner disclosure, software versions in response headers
Weak TLS configuration, certificate errors, no forward secrecy, mixed content
Open redirect on its own (out of scope on many programs)
User enumeration on its own (closed on most consumer platforms)
Autocomplete enabled, save-password allowed, plaintext password field, autocorrect enabled
No password policy, weak password policy, long session timeout, concurrent logins
Session not invalidated server-side only on logout; not invalidated on email or 2FA change
Reset token with a long expiry, or not invalidated after login or after a new request
OPTIONS or TRACE enabled
Internal IP disclosure, full path disclosure, descriptive stack trace
Publicly accessible robots.txt, GraphQL introspection enabled, missing SRI
Cookie scoped to the parent domain, missing HttpOnly on a non-session cookie
Missing CAA, missing DNSSEC, bitsquatting
A public CVE matched by version number only, with no verification on the target
Unpatched JavaScript libraries with no reachable sink
Raw, unvalidated scanner output (the single most common reason a report is closed)
Best-practice recommendations with no attack narrative
reporting_checklist: One finding per report, with the class named the way the program's taxonomy names it
Impact stated first, in the terms the business cares about: whose data, how many, what action, reversible or not
Reproduction that works from a clean session, with two accounts where the bug needs two
Minimal proof, not maximal exploitation. Read one record, not the table. Enumerate permissions read-only, never escalate further than needed to prove the class
The chain written out when it is a chain, with each link's own severity noted
No third-party or out-of-scope collateral, no DoS unless explicitly permitted, no data exfiltration beyond proof, nothing published
A concrete fix suggestion. It shortens triage and it is what separates a researcher from a scanner
